chunks: Say: 'We believe in God and what has been sent down to us, and what had been revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and their progeny, and that which was given to Moses and Christ, and to all other prophets by the Lord. We make no distinction among them, and we submit to Him.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to believe in all the prophets without distinction according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing the continuity of divine revelation, affirming that the core message of Islam has remained consistent across all prophets, from Abraham to Muhammad. It underscores the Shia principle of 'Tawhid' (monotheism) and 'Nubuwwah' (prophethood) by rejecting sectarian division among the children of Israel and emphasizing a unified submission to God. The phrase 'what was revealed to us' is often interpreted to include the Torah and Gospel in their original, uncorrupted forms, aligning with the belief in the authenticity of previous scriptures before their alteration.
